title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 120 (Maintenance and inspection of documents in electronic form)

content.overview: Without prejudice to any other provision of this Act, any document, record, register, minutes or books of any type required to be kept or maintained by a company under this Act may be kept or maintained in electronic form in such manner as may be prescribed.
content.glance: Electronic maintenance and inspection of prescribed company documents are permitted in the manner prescribed; the section does not waive the underlying record-keeping duty.
content.study:
## Section 120 — Electronic form

Section 120 permits documents, records, registers and minutes required to be kept by a company to be maintained and inspected in electronic form in the prescribed manner and subject to the prescribed conditions.

Check whether the record and company fall within the applicable rules; whether access, authentication, integrity, retention and inspection requirements are met; and whether the electronic version is available to the persons legally entitled to inspect it.

Section 120 changes the permitted form of maintenance or inspection; it does not remove the obligation to keep the record, expand inspection rights beyond the Act, or excuse compliance with the provisions governing the particular register, minutes or document.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

hypotheticals.question: Does keeping a register electronically remove the duty to allow legally required inspection?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 120 does not itself excuse underlying record-keeping or inspection obligations.
